subject: Maaplace - security briefing request and remediation update
messages:
From: Maaplace Security <security@maaplace.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Suspicious API usage — immediate review requested

Jonas,

We detected an unusual spike in API requests from a Maaplace integration key tied to one of our test environments. The requests originated from an IP we don't recognize and there are several 403/401 errors followed by successful requests. We're concerned this may indicate a leaked key or misconfigured client.

Could you please: 1) confirm whether any Redwood-hosted services show anomalous activity tied to our account, 2) share your incident response plan and a primary contact for SOC 2/incident escalation, and 3) provide any immediate mitigations you recommend while we investigate on our side?

We've attached an export of the initial access snapshot (maaplace_access_snapshot.json) and our internal alert trace. Please let us know if you need additional logs.

Thanks,
Aaron Rios
Head of Security Operations
Maaplace
Attachment: maaplace_access_snapshot.json (application/json, 14KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Maaplace Security <security@maaplace.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious API usage — immediate review requested

Aaron — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot. We're treating this as high priority. Immediate actions we're taking: 

- Revoking any active API keys tied to the Maaplace account until we confirm legitimacy.
- Collecting server-side request logs and token exchange events for the timeframe you provided.
- Standing up a private channel and scheduling a customer briefing.

I'm attaching our current incident response playbook (IR_Playbook_v2.1.pdf) and a stub export of the Redwood access logs we pulled this morning (sec_log_export_stub.txt). That log is an initial export — we'll deliver a fuller timeline after deeper triage.

Primary contacts: Hannah Schmitt (security ops) and Ben Carter (incident lead). Laura is on-copy for legal/contract questions. Marissa will coordinate the customer call.

Next steps for you: please confirm the exact API key IDs or client IDs you observed and whether you rotated keys on your side. We'll pause programmatic rotations while we correlate events.

I propose a 30-minute sync at 11:00 AM PT today to walk through findings; if that works, Marissa will send a calendar invite.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security (for Redwood Inference)
Redwood Inference
Attachment: IR_Playbook_v2.1.pdf (confidential)

From: Maaplace Security <security@maaplace.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Suspicious API usage — immediate review requested

Thanks, Jonas. We rotated the suspected key immediately after detection and can confirm the client_id is: mp-client-7129. We did not rotate our service account tokens. We also see outbound traffic to a third-party IP range during the window.

We've uploaded an extended set of traces to the Drive folder you referenced and added an initial timeline. We want clarification on whether any customer data (payloads) were returned or if this looks confined to auth/metadata.

Confirming the 11:00 AM PT sync — Marissa's calendar invite would be great.

-Aaron
Attachment: maaplace_extended_trace.zip (archive, stub referenced in Drive)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Preliminary triage notes (internal)

Team — quick summary from triage run overnight: 

- Root cause (initial): an onboarding script created a long-lived API key without scoped permissions. That key was stored in a shared test repo with lax access controls; third-party crawler likely discovered it.
- Containment: revoked the key at 2026-06-20T17:44:12Z; disabled the related service client; rotated backend tokens.
- Data exposure: at this stage we see requests for metadata and request headers; no evidence of payload-level exfiltration from Redwood-hosted storage. We are still scanning object-store logs and query traces to be certain.
- Next steps: full keystore scan for other long-lived keys, expedited review of onboarding script, and provide export of audited request logs for the customer.

I've attached preliminary triage notes for the call (prelim_triage_notes.docx). We'll finalize a sanitized summary for Maaplace that omits internal IDs and audit tokens.

Ben Carter
Senior Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachment: prelim_triage_notes.docx (internal)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Maaplace Security <security@maaplace.com>, A. Rios <aaron.rios@maaplace.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Bcc: compliance_reports@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 16:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Maaplace — incident summary and remediation plan (sanitized)

Aaron — attaching a sanitized incident summary and remediation plan for Maaplace (maaplace_sanitized_summary_20260622.pdf). Key points up front: 

- Timeline: initial anomalous activity detected 2026-06-20T08:58:00-07:00; customer reported at 09:12 PT; containment actions (key revoke + token rotations) completed by 2026-06-20T17:44:12Z.
- Scope: activity linked to a long-lived API key created by an onboarding script stored in a test repo. No confirmed exfiltration of payload data from Redwood-managed stores; request/metadata access observed.
- Remediation: we revoked the key, rotated tokens, updated onboarding scripts to enforce ephemeral keys and scoped permissions, and scheduled a keystore audit. We will also push an SDK update that prevents accidental commit of keys to public repos.
- Evidence: exported request logs and a redacted audit timeline are included in the Drive folder (link below).

Next steps for us: schedule a 45-minute technical debrief this week to walk Maaplace engineering through the sanitized timeline and logs. Laura is on-copy for contract/notification wording; she will confirm if this level of notification satisfies Maaplace's compliance needs while we finalize any SOC 2-affecting artifacts.

Links:
- Full redacted artifact folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_redwood/maaplace-incident-2026-06
- Requested HubSpot record: HS-82374

If you'd like an official SOC 2 artifact or SIG/CAIQ mapping affected by this event, we can prepare a targeted package — please indicate which you'd prefer (SOC 2 SIG mapping / audit copies / CAIQ response).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments: maaplace_sanitized_summary_20260622.pdf (redacted customer-facing), IR_Playbook_v2.1.pdf (reference)
